newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Glencar consolidates Wassa project in Ghana.
newsitem.headline: Glencar consolidates Wassa project in Ghana.

text.p: Glencar Explorations Plc said on Wednesday that it had consolidated its position in the Wassa project in Ghana by acquiring equity to gain control of Wassa Holdings.
The company said an intensive exploration programme had commenced and it expected that a feasibility study would be completed by mid 1997.
Glencar said exploration was continuing at Kanyankaw under the direction of Cyprus Amax while it was commencing an exciting exploration programme over a large area of prospective ground in Uganda.
"The next twelve months promises to provide a lot of interest and solid progress," chairman Richard Hooper said.
Glencar reported a pre-tax loss of 36,967 Irish pounds for the six months to June 30, 1996 compared to a pre-tax loss of 39,114 punts the previous year.

Glencar said further consolidation of the corporate ownership structure of Wassa Holdings had been achieved, culminating in the recently completed acquisition of the 15.7 percent interest in Wassa Holdings which had been held by the Emerging Markets Gold Fund.
Glencar said it now owned 61 percent of Wassa Holdings Limited, the balance being held by Moydow Limited.
Moydow Limited had indicated that it wishes to hold and fund its 39 percent interest in Wassa for the foreseeable future.
Glencar said its arbitration with MEV, the Hungarian uranium producer, was taking place in London at present and was due to conclude shortly.
It said its claim against MEV was for a total sum of approximately $3 million.

On the domestic front, Glencar said further drilling would be carried out on the Navan zinc/lead property before the end of this year while further detailed geochemical and geophysical studies were being carried out in the Kildare Block of licences.
